messages:
From: Elaine Wong <elaine@aurora.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot plan + MAP for GPU reservation (Aurora)

Aisha / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Leadership liked the latency profiles but wants a clear MAP and trial-to-commit path before we move budget. High level ask: we want a 6-week pilot on a 16-GPU pool (for inference and some eval sampling), then a staged ramp to 64 GPUs over 3 quarters. Key concerns: pricing tiers during ramp, short-term burst capacity for seasonal test runs, and a clear SLA/credits if latency targets slip.

Can you send a MAP that ties milestones to pricing/commits and explicitly calls out burst mechanics (how many GPUs, pricing, and preemption rules)? Also, the procurement team prefers a 12-month term but will consider a shorter initial commitment if there are defined conversion milestones.

Attaching our internal SOW template for reference.

Best,
Elaine
CTO, Aurora Robotics

Attachment: aurora-sow-template.docx (docx)

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Elaine Wong <elaine@aurora.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot plan + MAP for GPU reservation (Aurora)

Hi Elaine —

Thanks — and great to see the team engaged. I put together a working MAP that maps the 6-week pilot into decision milestones and ties each milestone to pricing and commit options. Summary of the proposal (details in the attached Aurora_MAP_v3.xlsx):

- Pilot (Weeks 0–6): 16-GPU dedicated pool, fixed pilot rate (30% off published slab price), includes 5 trial burst-hours/month up to +8 GPUs, no long-term commitment.
- Convert (By week 8): If Aurora signs the conversion notice, a tailored staircase commit kicks in: 32 GPUs (Q1), 48 GPUs (Q2), 64 GPUs (Q3). Commit terms default to 12 months from conversion; we offer a step-down for early termination tied to remaining months.
- Pricing ramps: volume-discount bands at 32/48/64 GPUs with progressive discounts (10%/15%/20%) off published per-GPU token pricing. Discounts applied on committed utilization baseline.
- Burst clauses: Burst up to 1.5x committed capacity for up to 48 hours/month at a higher per-hour rate; emergency bursts beyond that require pre-approval and are on a best-effort basis. Bursts are subject to transient preemption if region capacity constraints occur; guaranteed minimum of 90% of the committed pool during business hours.
- SLA & credits: 99.5% uptime SLA on committed pool with graduated credits (5–20%) for rolling monthly underperformance.

Next steps I propose: internal review with procurement + technical sizing call with Ben (to validate the 16->64 GPU transitions and estimated token economics). If that looks good, we’ll provide a short SOW + DocuSign link for the conversion notice.

I attached the MAP spreadsheet and a rough GPU sizing CSV Ben generated. Let me know if you want a one-page executive summary for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot plan + MAP for GPU reservation (Aurora) — sizing notes

Elaine / Aisha —

Quick technical notes from the sizing exercise (see gpu-sizing-estimate.csv for calculations):

- Pilot baseline: 16 x A100-equivalent for inference with room for KV cache headroom. At typical request mix (40% long-form, 60% short), we estimate 320M tokens/day at peak. The 16-GPU pool with continuous batching and prefix caching should meet the 95th-pct latency target (<=220 ms) during business hours.
- Ramp plan: primary gating criteria for moving from 16->32 is sustained 70% utilization over two consecutive weeks + agreed eval pass-rate (no more than 3% regression on chosen prompts).
- Burst implementation: we recommend using an isolated transient pool (not shared with customers) to avoid noisy neighbors. Implementation options: pre-provisioned burst slice (preferred) or dynamic cloud burst (cheaper but preemptible). Pricing differs by ~45% between these options during burst hours.
- Cost mitigation: enable KV prefix caching on high-frequency prompt families and token-level repacking to lower per-token GPU time — can save ~12–18% on incremental costs.

I can walk Aurora infra through the micro-benchmarks next Thursday if that helps accelerate technical signoff.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: gpu-sizing-estimate.csv (csv)

Aisha —

This is helpful, thanks. Procurement pushed back on the 12-month default on conversion; their preference is a 6-month step-up commitment after conversion with an optional 12-month auto-roll if utilization targets are met. They also want the first-quarter discount accelerated if we hit 50% of committed utilization in the pilot — essentially an early-adopter incentive.

Two asks before we move to SOW: 1) can you carve out a pre-provisioned burst slice for Aurora for the pilot (we'll accept the higher burst rate) so we can validate the scale without being preempted; 2) please provide a clear conversion notice language that toggles the staircase commit and the early-adopter discount condition.

If you send a redlineable SOW and the conversion notice text I’ll run it through procurement next week.

Regards,
Elaine

(Forwarded: aurora-procurement-questions.pdf)

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Elaine Wong <elaine@aurora.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot plan + MAP for GPU reservation (Aurora) — next steps and conversion language

Elaine —

Appreciate the quick feedback. We can support both asks. Summary of agreed updates (attached SOW draft and updated MAP spreadsheet):

- Pilot: include a pre-provisioned burst slice of +8 GPUs for the pilot window (these GPUs are reserved for Aurora; billed at burst rate).
- Conversion term: we’ll adopt a 6-month step-up commitment by default. If Aurora meets the utilization trigger (>=50% of aggregate committed baseline) within the pilot or first 30 days post-conversion, the contract automatically converts to a 12-month term with the accelerated first-quarter discount applied. The conversion notice language is below and I’ve added it to the SOW:  

Conversion Notice (proposed language): 
"Customer may elect to execute a Conversion Notice within 60 days of Pilot completion to initiate the Staircase Commitment. The Conversion Notice specifies initial committed capacity and an effective start date. If Customer achieves 50% or greater of the agreed committed baseline during the Pilot or within 30 days following Conversion Notice effective date, Redwood will apply the Accelerated Discount for the first billing quarter and extend the Commitment Term to 12 months from the Conversion effective date. Failure to meet the 50% utilization trigger will leave the Commitment Term at six (6) months unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

- Burst preemption / SLA language: pre-provisioned burst slice will not be preempted except for extreme force-majeure; dynamic bursts remain preemptible. We updated SLA credits matrix and added an emergency escalation path.

I attached a redlineable SOW and the MAP spreadsheet; Marissa and Ben helped with the edits. If that looks good, I’ll generate the DocuSign conversion notice and SOW and route to your procurement.

Next steps: confirmation from procurement by next Wednesday to stay on the close timeline and a technical review meeting Thurs 12/2 with Ben.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—Aisha
